name: Ridgepoint Tower
summary: Stormwind guards watch the eastern frontier from Ridgepoint Tower. They keep vigil over the perilous corridors, valleys, and roads leading into neighboring wilderness.

sections.title: Sentinel of the Eastern Border
sections.body: At Ridgepoint Tower, the garrison watches the valleys and roads of eastern Elwynn. The tower stands on high ground, where Stormwind's authority reaches its eastern border and the wilds begin. Its guards keep watch over the routes before threats can reach the farms and settlements nearer Northshire and Goldshire.

sections.title: Threats on Every Horizon
sections.body: Ridgepoint Tower faces threats from several directions. East lie the Redridge Mountains, where aggressive gnoll packs and blackrock orc raiders test human defenses. Across the southern river, undead horrors prowl the timberline of Duskwood. Rogue Defias Brotherhood bandits also haunt nearby wilderness camps, looking for gaps in the guard's defenses.

faq.answer: Ridgepoint Tower is a fortified scout tower in eastern Elwynn Forest, where the Stormwind Guard watches for hostile incursions and works to protect the kingdom.

faq.q: Who controls and mans the tower?
faq.answer: Guardsmen and scouts loyal to the Kingdom of Stormwind hold and garrison the tower. They operate under the command of the Stormwind Guard.

faq.q: What threats does the garrison watch out for?
faq.answer: The garrison watches for aggressive gnoll packs and blackrock orc raiders from the Redridge Mountains, undead horrors from Duskwood, and Defias Brotherhood bandits in nearby wilderness camps.
Ridgepoint Tower stands on high ground in eastern Elwynn Forest, near the borders of the Redridge Mountains and Duskwood.

angles.text: As an Alliance traveler, you can take Ridgepoint Tower as a reassuring beacon of safety and order before crossing into the perilous passes of Redridge or the haunted roads of Duskwood.
As a warrior, you can respect the stoic resolve of the guardsmen holding this exposed border outpost against surrounding hostiles.
